doc.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003

title: Parents' love of swing and the Beatles generation gap
summary: His mother loved swing; his daughters preferred the Beatles and he banned them from his stereo.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And did your parents like the swing music of the day too?

Oh absolutely. My mother was nuts about it. And she would say, “see the way he’s playing?” She said, “he’s so smooth and he smiles, but he’s got another thing, that umph.” She’d call it umph. He’s got a lot of umph.
That’s neat. It’s funny nowadays, I think for a while there’s been a separation between children and adults as far as their musical tastes.

Well probably. There was certainly a big disparaging thing in this house. I have a magnificent — I treated myself when I finally started making a little decent money — I treated myself to a marvelous stereo system for upstairs, all McIntosh, and big JBL studio monitor speakers, and oh what a system. It’s still up there. It’s never been played above 4 it’s so powerful. So anyway my kids started, the girls, both of my girls, they’re about six years apart, but it was The Beatles, you know when The Beatles started. And I’d say,

“how can you listen to that?” I said, “that’s terrible. It’s like nursery rhymes set to music. You could sing ‘Three Blind Mice’ like that. Terrible music.” Well naturally The Beatles were The Beatles and that’s all — the kids are walking up and down the street singing The Beatles songs. Nobody’s singing Benny Goodman licks anymore. But anyway I should have realized the handwriting on the wall at that time back then but I was stubborn. And I said, “you can’t play that stuff on my machine. Play it up in the bedroom on your stuff. You can’t do it on my stuff.” So they had to play theirs upstairs.
Did they have any sense that you used to be in the middle of what was swinging popular music? Did they realize that?
